extracted.intended_audience: citizens, stakeholders, students, and others interested in participating in federal rulemaking or learning how regulation is developed
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members of the public and stakeholders on how to participate in federal rulemaking (notice-and-comment), including when and how to submit feedback, other engagement opportunities, and where to find background resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) or Advanced Notice (ANPRM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies typically issue a 'notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM), or even an advanced notice of proposed rulemaking (ANPRM)' to solicit public feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the formal procedural vehicle through which agencies seek input; monitor Federal Register postings for NPRMs/ANPRMs to know when you can comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard comment period length
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard comment period lasts at least 60 days, though timelines vary by rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to submit comments within the designated period and confirm the specific deadline for each rulemaking because some proceedings use longer or shorter periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit written comments during designated periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties can submit written comments during designated periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written comments are the primary method for public input on NPRMs; ensure comments are timely and filed according to the instructions in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request individual meetings with agency representatives and OIRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties can request individual meetings with agency representatives and the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meetings provide an opportunity for direct engagement beyond the written record; requests should be made to the appropriate contacts and may supplement but not replace formal comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend public hearings when held
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public can attend public hearings when agencies hold them as part of the rulemaking process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public hearings offer another venue to present views orally; check the notice for hearing logistics and any requirements to register or submit testimony in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge final rules through congressional resolutions or litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules can be challenged through congressional resolutions or by filing litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dissatisfied with a final rule, stakeholders may pursue legal challenges in court or seek congressional action (e.g., disapproval resolutions) as remedies after rule issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the roles of the three branches in rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative: Congress creates the regulatory framework and delegates authority to agencies; Executive: agencies draft, propose, and finalize rules through established procedures; Judicial: courts review cases challenging agency implementations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing which branch performs which function helps identify appropriate avenues for influence and recourse (e.g., legislative change, administrative comment, judicial review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that the rulemaking process is not linear and requires active engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The process 'isn't a clear-cut, linear one' and the center encourages active civic engagement in rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective participation may require ongoing involvement across stages (pre-proposal outreach, formal comment, meetings, hearings, and post-finalization actions); be persistent and adaptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult available educational resources (e.g., Regulation: A Primer)
rubrics_metrics.description: The center offers 'Regulation: A Primer' and extensive educational materials on regulatory theory and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these resources (available in English and Korean) to build background knowledge on procedures, terminology, and strategic considerations before engaging in a rulemaking.
